title: Atom audit
intro: {n} short cards. Each one describes a single thing our system measures from a violin performance (we call it an "atom"). Rate each card on two questions and add a note if you like. There are no right answers; we want your judgment as a teacher.

questions.h1: Is this something violin teachers actually attend to in lessons?
questions.h2: If a tutor reported this value to a student, could the student act on it?
questions.h2_gloss: The number itself, not the concept: for example "your bow speed varied a lot in this phrase", as opposed to a quantity that no instruction maps to.

ui.calibration: Calibration example: rate it like any other card.
ui.note_prompt: Notes (optional): how would you say this to a student? Anything unclear?
ui.unanswered: Please answer both questions to continue.
ui.finish_text: All cards answered. Download your answers and send the file to Siyuan.
ui.send_hint: Please send the downloaded file to Siyuan by email or through the shared Dropbox folder.
ui.saved_hint: Your answers are saved in this browser as you go; you can close the page and come back.
ui.print_title: Printable form (paper fallback): cards in fixed order, tick one box per question.
ui.bullet_time: About 30 minutes, one card at a time.
ui.bullet_saved: Your answers save automatically in this browser; you can stop and come back later.
ui.bullet_send: At the end you download one file and send it to Siyuan.
ui.scale_note: No midpoint, on purpose: please lean one way.
ui.keys_hint: Keys 1 to 4 answer the next open question; Enter moves on.
ui.note_placeholder: Optional: how would you say this to a student? Anything unclear?

rows.name: Contact point, relative to the player's usual

phrases.source: Fischer, The Violin Lesson (2013)
Flesch, The Art of Violin Playing, Book 1

phrases.text: the bow drifting from the contact point
phrases.source: Starr, The Suzuki Violinist

phrases.text: evenness (from Lin Yaoji's maxim: evenness, accuracy, beauty; translated)
phrases.source: Lin Yaoji, teaching maxim, in Yang Baozhi, Essentials of Lin Yaoji's Violin Teaching Method (2004)

rows.definition: Where the bow hair touches the string between the bridge and the fingerboard, compared with the player's own usual contact point in that recording.
rows.unit: a fraction of the string length (bridge to nut)
rows.range: 0 = the player's usual point; negative = closer to the bridge than usual; positive = closer to the fingerboard than usual

rows.name: Position along the bow, frog to tip

phrases.text: at the frog / in the middle / at the tip

phrases.source: ViolinITS etude classification spreadsheet, columns "Equal length, 2 bow length, 3-4 bow length"
Fischer, The Violin Lesson (2013)

rows.definition: Which part of the bow hair is on the string at that moment, from the frog to the tip.
rows.unit: a fraction of the bow-hair length
rows.range: 0 = at the frog; 0.5 = the middle of the bow; 1 = at the tip

rows.name: Bow-to-string gap, on or off the string

phrases.text: bow on the string / off the string
Sautillé & Spiccato, Ricochet, Flying staccato (off-string strokes)
phrases.source: ViolinITS etude classification spreadsheet

rows.definition: How far the bow hair is from the string: zero when the bow is on the string, larger when it is lifted off.
rows.unit: a fraction of the string length
rows.range: 0 = hair on the string; larger = further off the string

rows.name: Bow skew: straight versus crooked bow

phrases.source: Hamann & Gillespie, Strategies for Teaching Strings (4th ed., 2018)
Provenzale et al. (2024), Sensors

rows.definition: How far the bow is from being at a right angle to the string, that is, how crooked the bow is.
rows.unit: degrees
rows.range: 0 = perfectly straight bow; larger = more crooked, whichever way it leans

rows.name: Bow tilt around the string: which string the bow is on

phrases.source: Galamian, Principles of Violin Playing and Teaching (1962); Rolland, The Teaching of Action in String Playing (1974)
Provenzale et al. (2024), Sensors

rows.definition: The angle at which the bow sits around the string, which shows which string the bow is leaning toward, measured against the violin body.
rows.unit: degrees
rows.range: an angle; smaller toward the G-string side, larger toward the E-string side

rows.name: Bow speed, with direction

phrases.source: Fischer, The Violin Lesson (2013); Flesch, The Art of Violin Playing, Book 1

phrases.text: It is impossible to scratch if the bow keeps moving
phrases.source: Fischer, The Violin Lesson (2013), chapter heading

phrases.text: evenness, accuracy, beauty (Lin Yaoji's three-word maxim, translated)
phrases.source: Lin Yaoji, teaching maxim, in Yang Baozhi, Essentials of Lin Yaoji's Violin Teaching Method (2004)

rows.definition: How fast the bow is moving along the string, with the sign showing whether it is a down-bow or an up-bow.
rows.unit: bow-hair lengths per second, so 1 means a whole bow in one second
rows.range: 0 = bow stopped; positive = down-bow (toward the tip); negative = up-bow

rows.name: Bow speed: how fast, regardless of direction

phrases.source: Fischer, The Violin Lesson (2013); Flesch, The Art of Violin Playing, Book 1
Fischer, The Violin Lesson (2013), chapter heading

rows.definition: How fast the bow is moving, regardless of whether it is a down-bow or an up-bow.
rows.unit: bow-hair lengths per second
rows.range: 0 = stopped; 1 = a whole bow in one second; larger = faster

rows.name: Bow acceleration

phrases.text: speeding up or slowing down the bow within a stroke

phrases.source: ViolinITS etude classification spreadsheet

rows.definition: How quickly the bow is speeding up or slowing down within a stroke.
rows.unit: change in bow speed per second
rows.range: 0 = steady speed; larger = the speed is changing faster; the sign follows the down-bow-positive convention

rows.name: Bow direction: down-bow or up-bow
rows.definition: Whether the bow is moving as a down-bow or an up-bow, as a smooth value that passes through zero when the bow changes direction.
rows.unit: a sign from −1 to +1
rows.range: +1 = clearly down-bow; −1 = clearly up-bow; near 0 = stopped or changing direction

rows.name: Right elbow bend (bow arm)

phrases.text: elbow angle / elbow height of the bow arm

phrases.source: Rolland, The Teaching of Action in String Playing (1974); Galamian, Principles (1962)

phrases.text: changing notes without changing the arm shape
phrases.source: Lin Yaoji, in Yang Baozhi (2004); English rendering only in our reading notes

rows.definition: How much the bow-arm elbow is bent, measured from the motion-capture model's straight-arm reference.
rows.unit: degrees of rotation from the reference pose, not a clinically calibrated joint angle
rows.range: 0 = arm straight in the reference pose; larger = more bent

rows.name: Right-wrist rotation, model axis X, relative to the player's usual

phrases.source: Rolland, The Teaching of Action in String Playing (1974)
ViolinITS schema leaf

phrases.text: how the wrist is turned about the model's X axis

rows.definition: One of three parts of how the bow-hand wrist is turned, taken about the motion-capture model's X axis, compared with this player's usual wrist posture in that recording. The three axes are the model's axes, not anatomical names such as flexion or deviation.
rows.unit: degrees
rows.range: 0 = the player's usual wrist posture in the recording; positive or negative = turned one way or the other about that axis

rows.name: Right-wrist rotation, model axis Y, relative to the player's usual

phrases.source: Rolland, The Teaching of Action in String Playing (1974)
ViolinITS schema leaf

phrases.text: how the wrist is turned about the model's Y axis

rows.definition: One of three parts of how the bow-hand wrist is turned, taken about the motion-capture model's Y axis, compared with this player's usual wrist posture in that recording. The three axes are the model's axes, not anatomical names such as flexion or deviation.
rows.unit: degrees
rows.range: 0 = the player's usual wrist posture in the recording; positive or negative = turned one way or the other about that axis

rows.name: Right-wrist rotation, model axis Z, relative to the player's usual

phrases.source: Rolland, The Teaching of Action in String Playing (1974)
ViolinITS schema leaf

phrases.text: how the wrist is turned about the model's Z axis

rows.definition: One of three parts of how the bow-hand wrist is turned, taken about the motion-capture model's Z axis, compared with this player's usual wrist posture in that recording. The three axes are the model's axes, not anatomical names such as flexion or deviation.
rows.unit: degrees
rows.range: 0 = the player's usual wrist posture in the recording; positive or negative = turned one way or the other about that axis

rows.name: Right shoulder rotation, relative to the player's usual

phrases.source: Rolland, The Teaching of Action in String Playing (1974)
Havas, A New Approach to Violin Playing (1961)

phrases.text: let the violin become part of the body (translated)
phrases.source: Lin Yaoji, in Yang Baozhi, Essentials of Lin Yaoji's Violin Teaching Method (2004)

rows.definition: How much the bow-arm shoulder is turned, compared with this player's usual shoulder position in that recording, in any direction.
rows.unit: degrees of rotation, not a clinically calibrated joint angle
rows.range: 0 = the usual shoulder position; larger = further from it

rows.name: Head and neck tilt

phrases.source: ViolinITS schema leaf

phrases.text: Analysis and correction of common posture errors in violin study (article title, translated)
phrases.source: Yang Lingchao (2001), article title

rows.definition: How far the head and neck are tilted away from the motion-capture model's upright reference, in any direction.
rows.unit: degrees
rows.range: 0 = the upright reference; larger = more tilted

rows.name: Spine curvature: upright versus slouched

phrases.source: Kreitman, Teaching from the Balance Point (1998); Flesch, The Art of Violin Playing, Book 1; Gruenberg (1919)
Rolland, The Teaching of Action in String Playing (1974)

rows.definition: How far the upper body is bent away from the motion-capture model's upright reference, combining the three spine joints.
rows.unit: degrees
rows.range: 0 = the upright reference; larger = more curved

rows.name: Violin hold height

phrases.source: Auer, Violin Playing as I Teach It (1921)

phrases.text: violin drifting over the right arm
phrases.source: Starr, The Suzuki Violinist
Rolland, The Teaching of Action in String Playing (1974)

phrases.text: let the violin become part of the body (translated)
phrases.source: Lin Yaoji, in Yang Baozhi, Essentials of Lin Yaoji's Violin Teaching Method (2004)

rows.definition: How high the violin's bridge sits above the player's hips, so a drooping violin gives a smaller value and a well-raised one a larger value.
rows.unit: a fraction of the string length, so it does not depend on body size
rows.range: larger = the violin is held higher relative to the hips

rows.name: Intonation error: sharp or flat

phrases.source: Galamian, Principles of Violin Playing and Teaching (1962)
Fischer, Basics (1997), section F heading
feedback wording in the experimental literature (Salzberg 1980)

phrases.text: intonation (the standard Chinese pedagogical term, translated)
phrases.source: Xiao Ke (2016); Ma Xishui (2002), article titles

phrases.text: accuracy (from Lin Yaoji's maxim: evenness, accuracy, beauty; translated)
phrases.source: Lin Yaoji, teaching maxim, in Yang Baozhi, Essentials of Lin Yaoji's Violin Teaching Method (2004)

rows.definition: How far the pitch actually played is from the written pitch of the note.
rows.unit: semitones; 100 cents make one semitone
rows.range: 0 = exactly the written pitch; positive = sharp; negative = flat; 0.5 = a quarter-tone off

rows.name: Loudness

phrases.text: dynamics (No dynamics, Simple Dynamics, Inter. dynamics)
phrases.source: ViolinITS etude classification spreadsheet, "Tone" columns
Auer, Violin Playing as I Teach It (1921), chapter topic

rows.definition: How loud the sound is at each moment, as the ear would hear it rise and fall.
rows.unit: decibels, a log scale of sound level
rows.range: higher = louder; very low = silence

rows.name: Note attack strength

phrases.source: Cavitt (2003), teacher correction targets (band rehearsals)
ViolinITS etude classification spreadsheet, "Bow strokes" columns
Fischer, Basics (1997), section C

phrases.text: attack / the start of the note

rows.definition: How strongly a new note is beginning at each moment: high at a clear, accented attack, low in the middle of a sustained note.
rows.unit: an attack-strength score with no physical unit
rows.range: 0 = no new note starting; larger = a stronger, sharper attack

rows.name: Pitch being played

phrases.source: Galamian, Principles of Violin Playing and Teaching (1962)
Hamann & Gillespie, Strategies for Teaching Strings (4th ed., 2018)

phrases.text: accuracy (from Lin Yaoji's maxim: evenness, accuracy, beauty; translated)
phrases.source: Lin Yaoji, teaching maxim, in Yang Baozhi, Essentials of Lin Yaoji's Violin Teaching Method (2004)

phrases.text: intonation (the standard Chinese pedagogical term, translated)
phrases.source: Xiao Ke (2016); Ma Xishui (2002), article titles

rows.definition: The pitch the violin is sounding at each moment, tracked continuously, so vibrato, slides and out-of-tune notes all show.
rows.unit: piano-key numbers with fractions; a step of 1 is one semitone
rows.range: higher = higher pitch, over the violin's range from the open G string upward

rows.name: Pitch clarity: how clearly a pitch is present

phrases.text: It is impossible to scratch if the bow keeps moving
phrases.source: Fischer, The Violin Lesson (2013), chapter heading
Hamann & Gillespie, Strategies for Teaching Strings (4th ed., 2018)
Suzuki, as described in Starr, The Suzuki Violinist

phrases.text: evenness, beauty (from Lin Yaoji's three-word maxim, translated)
phrases.source: Lin Yaoji, teaching maxim, in Yang Baozhi, Essentials of Lin Yaoji's Violin Teaching Method (2004)

rows.definition: How clearly a definite pitch is present in the sound at each moment: high for a clean, focused tone, low for scratch, noise or silence.
rows.unit: a pitch-evidence score with no physical unit
rows.range: near 0 = no clear pitch (silence or noise); larger = a clearer, more focused pitch

rows.name: Played on a different string than the score implies

phrases.text: wrong string / play it on the A string

phrases.source: ViolinITS etude classification spreadsheet, metadata column

phrases.text: building stepwise fingers on one string (D)
phrases.source: ViolinITS etude classification spreadsheet, goal text

rows.definition: How strongly the evidence from the sound and the left hand says the note was played on a different string from the one the written music implies.
rows.unit: a score from 0 to 1
rows.range: 0 = the same string as the score implies; 1 = clearly a different string; blank when the score gives no usable string

rows.name: Left-hand position, compared with what the score implies

phrases.source: Fischer, The Violin Lesson (2013), lesson topic; Fischer, Basics (1997), section E "Shifting"
ViolinITS etude classification spreadsheet, "Hand Frame" columns
Gerle, The Art of Practising the Violin (1983)
Ding Zhinuo, Intensive Training Materials for Violin Fundamentals (Shanghai Music Publishing House)

rows.definition: Where on the fingerboard the left hand actually was for the note, compared with the position the written music implies.
rows.unit: semitones along the string
rows.range: 0 = the position the score implies; positive = higher up the fingerboard than implied; negative = lower

rows.name: The player's habitual sounding point

phrases.source: Fischer, The Violin Lesson (2013)
Flesch, The Art of Violin Playing, Book 1

phrases.text: the bow drifting from the contact point
phrases.source: Starr, The Suzuki Violinist

phrases.text: evenness (from Lin Yaoji's maxim: evenness, accuracy, beauty; translated)
phrases.source: Lin Yaoji, teaching maxim, in Yang Baozhi, Essentials of Lin Yaoji's Violin Teaching Method (2004)

phrases.text: playing too close to the fingerboard / too close to the bridge

rows.definition: The player's usual contact point in that recording: where along the string the bow hair most often sits, between the bridge and the fingerboard.
rows.unit: a fraction of the string length (bridge to nut)
rows.range: 0 = at the bridge; larger = further toward the fingerboard; one value per recording, not per moment
